subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi's Day Schedule
hook: Can Ravi read the clock to find time for all his favorite activities?

slides.title: What Time Is It?
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks at the big clock on his classroom wall. 'Priya, what do all these numbers and hands mean? I want to know when recess is!'

points.label: The clock
points.text: Clock has numbers 1-12 and two moving hands.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clocks tell us when things happen!

image.alt: What Time Is It? — Telling Time

slides.title: The Clock Face
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'Look! There are 12 numbers around the clock. Top is 12. Right side is 3. Bottom is 6. Left is 9.'

points.label: Positions
points.text: 12 at top, 3 on right, 6 at bottom, 9 on left.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clock numbers are arranged in a circle!

image.alt: The Clock Face — Telling Time

slides.title: The Two Hands
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'The short hand shows hours. The long hand shows minutes. Short moves slow, long moves fast!'

points.label: Hands
points.text: Short hand = hours, Long hand = minutes

slides.inSimpleWords: Short hand is hours, long hand is minutes.

image.alt: The Two Hands — Telling Time

slides.title: Telling Hours
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'When the long hand points to 12 and the short hand points to 3, it's 3 o'clock!'

example.problem: If short hand is at 3 and long hand is at 12, what time is it?

slides.inSimpleWords: Short hand at 3, long hand at 12 = 3 o'clock.

image.alt: Telling Hours — Telling Time

slides.title: Another Hour
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees the short hand at 9 and long hand at 12. 'That's 9 o'clock! School time!' he shouts.

example.problem: Short hand at 9, long hand at 12. What time?

slides.inSimpleWords: 9 o'clock: short hand points to 9.

image.alt: Another Hour — Telling Time

slides.title: Reading Minutes
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Each small mark on the clock is one minute. 5 marks = 5 minutes. When the long hand is at 3, it's 15 minutes!'

points.label: Minutes
points.text: Long hand at 3 = 15 minutes. At 6 = 30 minutes. At 9 = 45 minutes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand shows: 0, 5, 10, 15... minutes.

image.alt: Reading Minutes — Telling Time

slides.title: Half Past
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'When the long hand points to 6, it's half past the hour! Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes!'

example.problem: If it's 2 o'clock and the long hand moves to 6, what time is it now?

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand at 6 = half past (30 minutes).

image.alt: Half Past — Telling Time

slides.title: Ravi's Schedule
slides.storyContext: Priya writes Ravi's day: School starts at 9:00. Recess at 11:00. Lunch at 1:00. Home at 3:00. 'Read each time on the clock!'

points.label: Schedule
points.text: 9:00 - School. 11:00 - Recess. 1:00 - Lunch. 3:00 - Home.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clocks help us organize our day!

image.alt: Ravi's Schedule — Telling Time

slides.title: Quarter Past
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'When the long hand points to 3, it's quarter past! That's 15 minutes after the hour.'

example.problem: It's 4 o'clock. The long hand moves to 3. What time now?

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand at 3 = quarter past (15 minutes).

image.alt: Quarter Past — Telling Time

slides.title: What Time for Play?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'If school ends at 3:00 and play time is half an hour later, what time is play?' Priya helps: 3:00 + 30 minutes = 3:30!
slides.inSimpleWords: Add minutes to know future times!

image.alt: What Time for Play? — Telling Time

slides.title: Time Mastered!
slides.storyContext: Ravi now reads the clock easily. 'I know hours and minutes! I can find time for school, recess, lunch, and play!'

points.label: Review
points.text: 1. Clock has 12 numbers. 2. Short hand = hours. 3. Long hand = minutes. 4. At 12 = top of hour. 5. At 3 = quarter past (15 min). 6. At 6 = half past (30 min). 7. At 9 = quarter to (45 min).

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading a clock helps plan your day!

image.alt: Time Mastered! — Telling Time

subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya's Garden Discovery
hook: What makes a plant different from a stone?

slides.title: The Garden Walk
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya walk into Priya's garden. 'Ravi, look around! This garden has living things and non-living things. Can you spot them?'

points.label: The garden
points.text: Plants, insects, stones, water, soil, and more!

slides.inSimpleWords: Nature has living AND non-living things.

image.alt: The Garden Walk — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: What Are Living Things?
slides.storyContext: Priya picks a green plant. 'This plant grows! It needs water, sunlight, and soil. It's alive! We call it a living thing.'

points.label: Living things
points.text: Grow, need food/water, can move, make babies, breathe.

slides.inSimpleWords: Living things grow and need food!

image.alt: What Are Living Things? — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Plants Are Living
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees tomato plants with red tomatoes. 'Priya, look! The flowers became tomatoes! Plants make babies!'

example.problem: Why is a tomato plant living?
example.solution: It grows, needs water, makes fruits (babies), and breathes through leaves.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants are living because they grow!

image.alt: Plants Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Animals Are Living
slides.storyContext: A butterfly lands on the flower. 'See this butterfly? It eats, it moves, it breathes. Animals are living things too!'

points.label: Animals
points.text: Eat food, move around, breathe, have babies, feel things.

slides.inSimpleWords: Animals are living because they move and eat!

image.alt: Animals Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: More Animals
slides.storyContext: Ravi finds an ant carrying food. An earthworm in the soil. A sparrow singing. 'So many living animals!'

example.problem: Are ants, worms, and birds living things?
example.solution: Yes! They all eat, move, breathe, and have babies. They are living.

slides.inSimpleWords: Ants, worms, birds all are living!

image.alt: More Animals — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: What Are Non-Living Things?
slides.storyContext: Priya picks up a stone. 'Now look at this rock. It doesn't grow. It doesn't eat. It doesn't move by itself. This is non-living.'

points.label: Non-living things
points.text: Don't grow, don't need food, don't breathe, don't move by themselves.

slides.inSimpleWords: Non-living things don't grow or eat!

image.alt: What Are Non-Living Things? — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Water and Soil
slides.storyContext: Ravi fills a bucket with water from the well. Priya says, 'Water and soil are non-living. We use them, but they're not alive.'

example.solution: Water is non-living. It doesn't grow or eat, but plants need it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water and soil are non-living helpers!

image.alt: Water and Soil — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Spot the Difference
slides.storyContext: Priya points to different things. 'That tree? Living. That wood chair? Non-living, because the tree is cut down now.'

points.label: Learning
points.text: Wood from a tree becomes a chair (non-living once cut).

slides.inSimpleWords: Cut wood stops being alive!

image.alt: Spot the Difference — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Humans Are Living
slides.storyContext: Ravi points to himself. 'Are we living things, Priya?' She nods. 'Yes! You eat, breathe, grow, and move. You're very alive!'

example.problem: Is a human a living thing?
example.solution: Yes! Humans grow, eat, breathe, feel, and have children. We are the most complex living things!

slides.inSimpleWords: We are living things too!

image.alt: Humans Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Make Two Lists
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Ravi, let's make a list. Living: plants, butterflies, ants, worms, birds, us. Non-living: stones, water, soil, air, wood, plastic.'

points.label: Organizing
points.text: Living and non-living both are part of nature!

slides.inSimpleWords: We can sort things into two groups!

image.alt: Make Two Lists — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Garden Lesson Complete
slides.storyContext: As the sun sets, Ravi and Priya sit. 'Everything in this garden—plants, animals, stones, water—works together. The living needs the non-living!'

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Living things grow, eat, breathe, move. 2. Non-living things don't. 3. Both are important. 4. Together they make nature beautiful. 5. We are living and part of nature!

slides.inSimpleWords: Living things and non-living things work together!

image.alt: Garden Lesson Complete — Living and Non-Living

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi and Priya's Animal Adventure
hook: Where does a bird sleep? Where does a fish rest?

slides.title: Different Houses, Different Animals
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya explore nature. 'Priya, do all animals live in the same kind of home?' Priya smiles. 'No! Each animal has its own perfect home!'

points.label: Discovery
points.text: Animals live in different places based on what they need.

slides.inSimpleWords: Different animals have different homes!

image.alt: Different Houses, Different Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Nests for Birds
slides.storyContext: Priya points to a nest in a tree. 'See this nest? Birds build it from twigs and grass. They lay eggs here and raise babies!'

points.label: Bird homes
points.text: Birds live in nests in trees, bushes, rocks, or holes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Birds make nests in trees!

image.alt: Nests for Birds — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Different Bird Nests
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees many nests. 'Some are round, some are messy, some are tiny!' Priya says, 'Each bird builds its own style of nest!'

example.solution: In a nest made of grass and twigs in a tree or on a building.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sparrows nest in trees and buildings!

image.alt: Different Bird Nests — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Holes for Small Animals
slides.storyContext: Priya shows a burrow in the ground. 'Rabbits and squirrels dig holes called burrows. Underground is safe and cool!'

points.label: Underground homes
points.text: Rabbits, squirrels, moles, and frogs live in holes and burrows.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some animals dig holes underground!

image.alt: Holes for Small Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Ant Hill and Beehive
slides.storyContext: Ravi finds an anthill. 'Look at all those tunnels!' Then Priya shows a beehive in a tree. 'Ants and bees build amazing homes together!'

example.solution: In anthills with tunnels underground. Many ants live and work together.

slides.inSimpleWords: Ants live in hills; bees live in hives!

image.alt: Ant Hill and Beehive — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Water Homes
slides.storyContext: They visit a pond. Priya says, 'Fish live in water. Frogs also live here. Even snakes can hide in water!'

points.label: Aquatic homes
points.text: Fish, frogs, turtles, and water snakes live in ponds, rivers, lakes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fish and frogs live in water!

image.alt: Water Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Shells and Coral Homes
slides.storyContext: Priya shows a snail shell. 'This snail carries its home! Crabs have hard shells too. In the sea, fish hide in coral!'

example.solution: In its hard shell, which it carries everywhere as protection.

slides.inSimpleWords: Snails carry their homes!

image.alt: Shells and Coral Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Dens and Caves
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Do big animals like lions live in homes too?' Priya nods. 'Lions live in caves or dens. Tigers hide in forests. Elephants roam wide areas.'

points.label: Big homes
points.text: Lions: caves/dens. Tigers: forests. Elephants: grasslands.

slides.inSimpleWords: Big animals live in caves and forests!

image.alt: Dens and Caves — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Homes Protect Animals
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Homes keep animals safe from danger. Nests keep baby birds warm. Burrows keep rabbits from predators.'

example.problem: Why does a rabbit live in a burrow?
example.solution: Underground is safe from predators and keeps them cool in summer, warm in winter.

slides.inSimpleWords: Homes keep animals safe and comfy!

image.alt: Homes Protect Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Match Animals to Homes
slides.storyContext: Ravi tries to match: 'Sparrow → nest, fish → water, squirrel → hole, lion → cave!' Priya claps, 'Perfect!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Different animals, different homes. All perfectly suited!

slides.inSimpleWords: Each animal picks the best home!

image.alt: Match Animals to Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Animal Homes Tour Ends
slides.storyContext: As they walk home, Ravi realizes, 'Every animal has a home made just for it! Birds in nests, fish in water, rabbits in holes. Nature is amazing!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Birds live in nests. 2. Small animals in burrows/holes. 3. Fish and frogs in water. 4. Big animals in caves/forests. 5. Homes keep animals safe. 6. Each home is perfectly suited to that animal!

slides.inSimpleWords: Every animal has a perfect home!

image.alt: Animal Homes Tour Ends — Animals and Their Homes
